paragraphs.text: Why Antarctic ozone fell 40 to 50 percent.
The question asks what would happen if the ozone hole kept growing, letting far more ultraviolet radiation reach the surface.
We assume that CFC emissions persisted without regulation, maintaining the pre‑Montreal trajectory of atmospheric chlorine loading.
Antarctic ozone fell 40 to 50 percent as chlorine from CFCs tore ozone apart, weakening the layer that absorbs ultraviolet light; without the ban, far more UV would reach the ground.
The governing physics is that chlorine released from CFCs catalytically destroys stratospheric ozone, which normally absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
Science cannot predict the exact timeline because it depends on how the impossible change occurs; only the order of effects is bounded by established physics.
